repaint.hintBrush: Drag over the part that may change
repaint.hintErase: Drag over a mark to take it back off
repaint.hintBox: Drag out a rectangle, corner to corner
repaint.hintOutline: Click around the part, then click the first point again to close it
repaint.note: Mark the part that may change. The rest is sent exactly as it is, and what the marking becomes is said in words beside it. The picture this node holds is left alone: the mask is filed next to it, wired into its mask port, and the run is one press away in the panel that opens.
repaint.unreadable: The picture cannot be read here, so there is nothing to mark on
repaint.markPrompt: Mark the part of the picture that may change
repaint.sayWhatItBecomes: Say what the marked part should become
repaint.cannotDraw: This window cannot draw a mask
repaint.nothingMarked: Nothing is left marked. A mask with nothing white in it asks for the whole picture to change, which is not a repaint.
repaint.maskNotWritten: The mask could not be written out
repaint.cannotShow: The picture cannot be shown here
repaint.maskSize: The mask will be {{width}} × {{height}} pixels — the size of the picture itself — and filed as {{name}}
repaint.whatItBecomes: What the marked part should become
repaint.becomesPlaceholder: A stone jetty running out into the water
repaint.noModel: No model is chosen yet, so which one this is asked through will decide whether the region can be held to
repaint.hasMaskField: This model has a field of its own for a mask, so what changes stays inside the marking
repaint.noMaskField: This model has no field of its own for a mask. It travels as a second picture beside the words, so what changes may not stay inside the marking — say which part of the picture is meant in the words as well.

describe.note: Ask a model to read this picture back as the words that would make it. The words become a text node of their own, wired into this picture's prompt, so they can be read, corrected and let go of on the canvas rather than hiding in a field — and the picture is one press from being generated again from them. This is an ask, and it costs what an ask costs.
describe.whatToAsk: What to ask about the picture
describe.sayWhatToAsk: Say what to ask about the picture
describe.nothingCameBack: Nothing came back to file. Ask in other words, or check that the model can see a picture at all.
describe.wordsNotFiled: The words could not be filed on this canvas
describe.pictureNotRead: The picture could not be read
describe.noModelChosen: No model is chosen for written answers, so there is nothing to ask
describe.modelGone: The model this would be asked through is gone, so there is nothing to ask
describe.askedThrough: Asked through {{display}} as {{model}}. A model that cannot see a picture will answer about the question alone, which reads as a description of nothing — Escape lets go of an answer still arriving.
describe.cannotShow: The picture cannot be shown here, but it is still sent as it is stored

pictureTool.purposeCrop: Cuts a region out and files it as a picture of its own. The picture this node holds is left exactly as it is.
pictureTool.purposeSplit: Divides the picture into pieces and files each one, in reading order
pictureTool.purposeResize: Resamples the pixels that are here. It can make a picture smaller cleanly, and larger only by guessing — a model is what adds detail.
pictureTool.purposeTilt: Turns the picture in perspective and files the plate, with the words that describe the shot beside it
pictureTool.cannotShow: The picture cannot be shown here. The numbers are still in its own pixels, and the tool works on the file itself.
pictureTool.pictureSize: {{width}} × {{height}} pixels. Every number here is in them, not in the size the node is drawn at.
pictureTool.overPixels: This picture is {{width}} by {{height}}, which is past the {{ceiling}} pixels one tool works on — make it smaller first
pictureTool.notAProportion: A proportion is two numbers with a colon between them, like 16:9
pictureTool.noRoomForProportion: A picture {{width}} by {{height}} has no room for that proportion
pictureTool.regionInsidePicture: A region is four whole numbers inside the picture, which is {{width}} by {{height}}
pictureTool.regionFourNumbers: A region is four whole numbers of pixels: how far in, how far down, how wide, how tall
pictureTool.divisionNumbers: A division is one whole number of rows and one of columns
pictureTool.divisionCeiling: {{count}} is as far as one division goes each way
pictureTool.sizeNumbers: A size is two whole numbers of pixels, at least one each way
pictureTool.targetPastCeiling: {{width}} by {{height}} is past the {{ceiling}} pixels one tool works on
pictureTool.turnCeiling: {{count}} degrees is as far as this turns
pictureTool.piecesNote: How many pieces, across and down
pictureTool.piecesMade: {{count}} pieces, filed in reading order and selected together, so they can be grouped the moment they land
pictureTool.onePieceMade: 1 piece, filed in reading order and selected together, so they can be grouped the moment they land
pictureTool.willBeResampled: The size it will be resampled to
pictureTool.largerThanSource: That is larger than the picture that is there, so the extra is guessed rather than remembered.
pictureTool.hintContain: The whole picture, as large as the box allows.
pictureTool.hintCover: The whole box, from the middle of the picture. What overflows is cut.
pictureTool.hintFill: The whole box, whatever that does to the shape.
pictureTool.tiltNote: A sketch of the turn rather than the pixels it will make. The plate keeps the picture's own size, and what the turn leaves see-through stays see-through — which is why it is filed as a PNG.
